citations.assessment: The named Mar Zutra occurs in company with Ashi in the Bavli; Sherira also names Mar Zutra among leaders in Ashi’s period, without identifying every Bavli occurrence.
The episode begins at Azgor’s gate on 61a and continues on 61b.

Ashi says he saw something else in the food before the examination and later tells the rabbis of a spirit of tsaraat. Heilprin paraphrases both as tsaraat. Preserve the distinction between the primary wording and his paraphrase.
The Bavli quotes the bedtime pardon under a bare Mar Zutra, leaving the patronymic unexpressed.
The Bavli explicitly has one sixtieth. This is a parallel to the phrase as quoted, without verifying the later work or its application.
Acha son of Rav Yosef reports the Mar Zutra–Pappa chain with Ashi’s ordering after Ashi objects to the first formulation.
The exact chain occurs in the ruling on a linen thread pulled from wool. The Bavli calls Acha the son of Rav Yeiva.
All three are together; Amemar and Rav Ashi ate the raw greens, while Mar Zutra declined. Read the general meal wording against that explicit distinction.
Ashi reports Zutra’s citation of Rav Chanina of Sura’s objection in the Torah-scroll discussion.
The independent passage concerns hair follicles and carries the same named chain.
Mar Zutra visited the house of Rav Ashi and saw the screen around the Torah scroll in the place of Mar bar Rav Ashi.
The Rav Zevid entry points to the daughter-in-law’s property dispute; the Bavli gives Mar Zutra, Amemar, Rav Ashi and Rav Gamda. Zevid appears in the relationship and Gamda’s challenge.
Mar Zutra expounds in Rav Huna’s name that one fasts and completes the fast.
This independently located parallel carries the same transmission.
The digital witnesses explicitly preserve both names in the rule for setting aside a corner for dirt.
Mar Zutra expounds in Rav Chisda’s name in the context of making a stringent ruling about one’s own food.

The specific acquisition concerns the convert’s enslaved servant, with differing accounts about age and consequent acquisition rules. Heilprin reports the incident generically as a property acquisition.
The Bavli gives Merimar or Rav Yeimar as alternatives and puts the visit in the first person. Heilprin’s compact wording gives both names.
The internal entry gives the precise lecture locus and names Mar Zutra as the addressee; the checked Bavli currently leaves the addressee implicit in this line.
Mar Zutra challenges Mesharshya’s assertion about Doeg and Achitophel.
The Pappa transmission concerns a mortgage in a place where one can redeem the property.
The disputed openings in the esophagus and gizzard have separately reported formulations in the name of Pappa.
Mar Zutra explicitly reports seeing Rav Pappi bless upon putting on tefillin.
Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi came before Rava bar Chinena in the slaughterer’s case.
Mar Zutra names Rav Sheshet as the source of the terumah ruling and the surrounding voice explicitly rules otherwise.
The Tosafot explicitly prefer Ashi in the named property dispute. Preserve its limited scope.
Rosh 1:40 explicitly rules like Ashi in this dispute, not a general rule for all his exchanges with Mar Zutra.
The cited Part 1 entry gives 4162–4170, eight years, as its own chronology and explicitly notes its source controversy.
